_comment: local_classify cases. The gold labels live in `expect.label_is`, not in prose.
They used to live in `human_review` strings — 'Correctness: the answer should be `bug`'
— while this comment and the README both claimed automating accuracy 'needs a labelled
set this repo does not have'. The set was right there, two lines away, in the wrong
column. On the live rows a 0.6B answered `feature request` where the gold was `bug` and
the row read mechanical_ok: true, because nothing was comparing them.
Three checks do different jobs here and the distinction matters:
label_is        — is the answer CORRECT (against the gold label)
category_member — is the answer a BARE LABEL from the offered list, as instructed
expect_row      — assertions about the row, e.g. matched:false on out-of-domain input
A model can be right and undisciplined ('I would say bug'), or disciplined and wrong.

cases.why: Issue #1 records this exact failure: a 0.6B model classified 'the effect size was too small and it disappeared after two weeks' as POSITIVE. The sentiment is negative and stated plainly; only the academic register is neutral. This is the regression case the issue asks for.

arguments.text: The effect size was too small and it disappeared after two weeks.

human_review: Issue #1 observed a 0.6B answering `positive` here. label_is now decides that; what is left for you is whether a wrong answer was a near miss (neutral) or an inversion (positive).
If category_member failed while label_is passed, the model was right but decorated its answer.

cases.why: The tool's prompt says 'Reply with the category name alone, copied exactly as written above.' Small models decorate ('Category: bug', 'I would say bug.'). The server matches decorated replies back onto the list, so `matched` stays true — which is why raw_response, not category, is what gets checked here.

arguments.text: The app crashes on launch whenever the config file is missing.

human_review: Compare `text` (the raw reply) with `category` (what the server matched it to). A gap between them is decoration the caller never asked for.
This is the case where a 0.6B answered `feature request`: correct-looking row, wrong answer, until label_is existed.

cases.why: Issue #1: 'Whether matched: false fires when it should.' Nothing in the offered list fits, so a well-behaved model has no honest bare label to give. The expectation is a ROW fact (matched must be false), not a text fact — scoring it with category_member pointed the verdict backwards: the desired outcome failed and forcing a label passed.
human_review: A forced label that matches is WORSE than an unmatched reply: it looks clean and is wrong. That is now a mechanical failure rather than a note.
There is no gold label here on purpose — the right behaviour is to name none of them.
